# Video Doc Generator

> A Python package that manages video links, calls video parsing APIs to read and parse videos, and converts video content into professional documents and analysis reports.

## Overview

Video Doc Generator provides video link management, video parsing, and document generation capabilities.

- **Package**: `pip install video-doc-generator`
- **Python**: 3.8+
- **Platforms**: Windows, macOS, Linux
- **License**: MIT

## Quick Start

### Installation

```bash
# Basic installation
pip install video-doc-generator

# With development dependencies
pip install video-doc-generator[dev]
```

### Basic Usage

```python
from video_doc_generator import VideoManager, VideoParser, DocumentGenerator

# 1. Manage video links
manager = VideoManager()
manager.add("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=example", title="Example Video")

# 2. Parse video
parser = VideoParser(api_key="your-api-key", api_url="https://api.example.com/video/parse")
result = parser.parse("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=example")

# 3. Generate document
generator = DocumentGenerator(output_dir="docs")
filepath = generator.generate_markdown(result)
```

## Core API Reference

### VideoManager Class

The main class for managing video links.

#### Constructor Parameters

```python
VideoManager(
    storage_path: Optional[str] = None,  # Storage file path, default: ~/.video_doc_generator/videos.json
)
```

#### Core Methods

```python
# Add a video link
video = manager.add(
    url: str,
    title: Optional[str] = None,
    metadata: Optional[Dict] = None,
) -> VideoLink

# Remove a video link
success = manager.remove(url: str) -> bool

# Get a video link by URL
video = manager.get(url: str) -> Optional[VideoLink]

# List all video links
videos = manager.list_all() -> List[VideoLink]

# Get video count
count = manager.count() -> int

# Clear all videos
manager.clear() -> None
```

### VideoParser Class

The class for parsing videos via API.

#### Constructor Parameters

```python
VideoParser(
    api_key: Optional[str] = None,      # API key from environment or parameter
    api_url: Optional[str] = None,      # API URL from environment or parameter
)
```

#### Core Methods

```python
# Parse video (synchronous)
result = parser.parse(video_url: str) -> VideoParseResult

# Parse video (asynchronous)
result = await parser.parse_async(video_url: str) -> VideoParseResult
```

#### Return Types

```python
class VideoMetadata(BaseModel):
    url: HttpUrl
    title: Optional[str] = None
    description: Optional[str] = None
    duration: Optional[int] = None  # seconds
    thumbnail: Optional[str] = None
    author: Optional[str] = None
    platform: Optional[str] = None

class VideoTranscript(BaseModel):
    text: str
    segments: Optional[list] = None
    language: Optional[str] = None

class VideoParseResult(BaseModel):
    metadata: VideoMetadata
    transcript: Optional[VideoTranscript] = None
    raw_data: Optional[Dict] = None
```

### DocumentGenerator Class

The class for generating documents from video content.

#### Constructor Parameters

```python
DocumentGenerator(
    output_dir: Optional[str] = None,  # Output directory, default: "docs"
)
```

#### Core Methods

```python
# Generate Markdown document
filepath = generator.generate_markdown(
    parse_result: VideoParseResult,
    filename: Optional[str] = None,  # Output filename, default: video title or timestamp
) -> Path
```

### VideoLink Class

Data model for video links.

```python
class VideoLink(BaseModel):
    url: HttpUrl
    title: Optional[str] = None
    platform: Optional[str] = None  # Auto-detected: youtube, bilibili, vimeo, unknown
    added_at: Optional[str] = None
    metadata: Optional[Dict] = None
```

## Command Line Interface

```bash
# Add a video link
video-doc add "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=example" --title "Example Video"

# List all videos
video-doc list

# Remove a video link
video-doc remove "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=example"

# Parse video and generate document
video-doc parse "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=example" --output-dir docs

# Process all added videos
video-doc process-all --output-dir docs
```

### CLI Options

```bash
# Parse command options
video-doc parse <url> \
    --output-dir <dir> \          # Output directory (default: docs)
    --api-key <key> \             # Video parser API key
    --api-url <url>               # Video parser API URL

# Process-all command options
video-doc process-all \
    --output-dir <dir> \          # Output directory (default: docs)
    --api-key <key> \             # Video parser API key
    --api-url <url>               # Video parser API URL
```

## Configuration

### Environment Variables

```bash
export VIDEO_PARSER_API_KEY="your-api-key"
export VIDEO_PARSER_API_URL="https://api.example.com/video/parse"
```

### Config Class

```python
from video_doc_generator import Config

config = Config()
config.video_parser_api_key      # API key
config.video_parser_api_url      # API URL
config.storage_dir               # Storage directory
config.videos_storage_path       # Videos storage file path
config.default_output_dir        # Default output directory
```

## Examples

### Example 1: Basic Usage

```python
from video_doc_generator import VideoManager, VideoParser, DocumentGenerator

# Manage video links
manager = VideoManager()
manager.add("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=example", title="Example Video")

# Parse video
parser = VideoParser(api_key="your-api-key")
result = parser.parse("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=example")

# Generate document
generator = DocumentGenerator(output_dir="docs")
filepath = generator.generate_markdown(result)
print(f"Document generated: {filepath}")
```

### Example 2: Batch Processing

```python
from video_doc_generator import VideoManager, VideoParser, DocumentGenerator

manager = VideoManager()
parser = VideoParser(api_key="your-api-key")
generator = DocumentGenerator(output_dir="docs")

# Process all videos
for video in manager.list_all():
    try:
        result = parser.parse(str(video.url))
        filepath = generator.generate_markdown(result)
        print(f"Processed: {filepath}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error processing {video.url}: {e}")
```

### Example 3: Async Parsing

```python
import asyncio
from video_doc_generator import VideoParser

async def parse_videos(urls):
    parser = VideoParser(api_key="your-api-key")
    tasks = [parser.parse_async(url) for url in urls]
    results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
    return results

urls = [
    "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=example1",
    "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=example2",
]
results = asyncio.run(parse_videos(urls))
```

## Key Imports

```python
from video_doc_generator import (
    Config,
    VideoManager,
    VideoParser,
    DocumentGenerator,
)

# Or import specific classes
from video_doc_generator.manager import VideoManager, VideoLink
from video_doc_generator.parser import VideoParser, VideoParseResult, VideoMetadata, VideoTranscript
from video_doc_generator.generator import DocumentGenerator
```

## Video Platform Detection

The VideoLink class automatically detects video platforms:

- **YouTube**: youtube.com, youtu.be
- **Bilibili**: bilibili.com
- **Vimeo**: vimeo.com
- **Unknown**: Other platforms

## Storage

Video links are stored in JSON format at:
- Default: `~/.video_doc_generator/videos.json`
- Custom: Specify `storage_path` in `VideoManager()` constructor
